overview: BLIS Technologies is a Dunedin, New Zealand-based, 25-year-old developer and commercialiser of proprietary oral probiotic bacterial strains, principally BLIS K12 (Streptococcus salivarius K12) and BLIS M18, sold both as an ingredient to third-party consumer-health brands (B2B, ~68% of FY26 revenue) and as BLIS's own finished consumer products (B2C, ~32%). Revenue is small and geographically diversified (North America 31%, EMEA 30%, Asia Pacific ex-NZ 24%, New Zealand 15% of FY26 revenue) but the company remains a nano-cap: after eight years growing revenue from $8.2m (FY19) to $14.7m (FY26), EBITDA margins are thin and volatile (6% in FY26, having been negative in FY22-23) and the market capitalisation is roughly NZ$20-23m at a ~$0.016-0.018 share price against 1.279 billion shares on issue.

business_model.summary: BLIS licenses/sells its patented probiotic strains as raw ingredients to third-party manufacturers (ingredient sales $7.29m FY26, +19%; royalty/licence revenue $1.25m FY26, +17%, earned as legacy ingredient customers -- notably Probi AB in North America -- transition to Probi's own manufacturing) and separately sells its own finished consumer products (capsules, lozenges, dental SKUs) through NZ pharmacy wholesale, Amazon US, its own webstore, and cross-border e-commerce (CBEC) into China. FY26 revenue was $14.668m, up 16% on FY25's $12.644m, but reported EBITDA was only $0.9m (6% margin) after absorbing a disclosed $0.9m one-off supply-chain cost increase; underlying (adjusted) EBITDA was $1.8m. NPAT was $0.7m. The single most important commercial relationship is with Probi AB, a Swedish probiotics company that is simultaneously BLIS's largest licensee/customer, a top-3 (12.99%) shareholder, and has a seat on the BLIS board (CEO Anita Johansen is a BLIS director) -- Probi-related-party revenue was $2.34m in FY26 (~16% of total revenue). Cash generated from operations was NEGATIVE $(0.6)m in FY26 (vs +$1.8m in FY25) despite positive NPAT, driven by an $862k inventory build (raw materials roughly tripled to $1.19m as BLIS pre-purchased stock through the disclosed supply-chain cost shock) and a $984k increase in trade receivables consistent with revenue growth and a large EMEA customer's order timing -- i.e. a genuine, one-off-flavoured working-capital drag rather than a structural cash-generation problem, but one that illustrates how quickly a small change in inventory/receivables can flip this business cash-flow negative.

revenue_streams.name: B2B ingredient sales (bulk BLIS K12/M18 to manufacturers)
B2B private label / royalty & licence fees (incl. Probi)
B2C New Zealand wholesale (pharmacy, dental SKUs)
Other income (interest, grants)
revenue_streams.trend: declining as cash balance is used for growth

business_model.customer_type: Mixed B2B (ingredient manufacturers, consumer-brand licensees, one dominant related-party partner in Probi AB) and B2C (pharmacy/wholesale retail, e-commerce/Amazon, direct webstore); highly customer-concentrated -- the three largest customers accounted for $7.99m of $14.67m FY26 revenue (~54%), versus ~54% in FY25 also
business_model.geographic_mix: North America 31% ($4.5m), EMEA 30% ($4.35m), Asia Pacific ex-NZ 24% ($3.57m), New Zealand 15% ($2.24m) of FY26 revenue; manufacturing and all non-current assets are based in New Zealand (Dunedin)

main_competitors: Probi AB (Sweden) -- both BLIS's largest licensee/distribution partner AND an increasingly capable direct competitor as it internalises manufacturing of BLIS-derived and its own probiotic strains
Chr. Hansen / Novonesis (Denmark, post-merger probiotics giant) -- global-scale ingredient supplier with vastly greater R&D and manufacturing scale
Generic/commodity oral-health probiotic strain suppliers (particularly from China) competing on price in the ingredient channel
Numerous smaller finished-goods consumer probiotic brands in the B2C oral-health and immunity categories
competitive_position.market_position: Niche specialist in oral-cavity probiotic strains (BLIS K12, M18) with a long clinical publication history (20 publications relating to its strains highlighted in FY26, 17 conferences attended/presented at) but tiny in absolute scale (~$14.7m revenue) relative to global probiotics/nutraceutical ingredient suppliers. BLIS is a price-taker in a market it does not lead by scale, and its own largest commercial partner (Probi) is progressively taking over manufacturing and distribution in BLIS's most lucrative territory (North America), converting BLIS from a product supplier into a lower-margin royalty recipient there.

moat_factors.factor: Patent portfolio and clinical evidence base
moat_factors.description: Two new patents granted in FY26 (antiviral applications of S. salivarius K12/M18, and prebiotic-sugar formulations), plus 20 publications relating to BLIS strains cited in FY26 and a 25-year track record of peer-reviewed clinical research (originating from Professor John Tagg's University of Otago research). This is a real, defensible scientific/IP asset relative to undifferentiated generic probiotic suppliers, and did prove valuable in FY26: BLIS successfully resolved a material patent dispute with Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan (joint ownership outcome) and separately received a favourable FDA 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS status) update in May 2026. However, patents are a wasting asset -- with 10-20 year amortisation lives disclosed in the accounts -- and BLIS's moat rests as much on trade secrets/know-how and its brand/publication reputation as on enforceable patent exclusivity, which is a materially weaker moat than a pharma-style composition-of-matter patent.

moat_factors.factor: Strategic distribution partnership with Probi AB
moat_factors.description: The October 2025 revised Technology Licence and Distribution Agreement extends Probi's EXCLUSIVE rights to BLIS K12/M18 across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets, and newly adds pet nutrition. This gives BLIS access to a much larger commercial partner's sales/marketing network, but the exclusivity itself concentrates BLIS's most valuable territories behind a single counterparty that also has board representation and is simultaneously reducing its ingredient purchases from BLIS as it internalises manufacturing (North America ingredient revenue fell $0.4m in FY26 as royalty revenue rose in its place) -- structurally this looks more like managed decline of direct control over BLIS's best markets than a growth moat.

BLIS K12 and M18 hold GRAS 'no objection' status with the FDA and various other jurisdictional approvals; the ongoing China regulatory pathway (a key clinical trial commenced in 2H26, expected complete 1H27) is a multi-year investment to unlock a large but currently CBEC/grey-market-dependent Chinese consumer opportunity. This is a genuine, hard-to-replicate barrier for new entrants but requires continuous capital and management attention, and BLIS's own FY26 letter flags 'progression... to examination stage' rather than approval.

BLIS relies on a single New Zealand fermentation supplier for its core strains; a technology/know-how transfer to an offshore fermentation supplier is underway specifically because the company has identified single-supplier concentration as a continuity risk. The FY26 result was directly hit by a disclosed $0.9m one-off supply chain cost increase, evidencing real operating fragility around a small manufacturing base.

weaknesses: Extreme revenue and profit concentration in three customers (~54% of FY26 revenue), one of which (Probi AB) is also a major shareholder and board-represented related party -- a structural conflict-of-interest and bargaining-power risk, not merely a diversification risk

Eight years to grow revenue from $8.2m to $14.7m (a ~9% CAGR) while EBITDA margin has oscillated between -24% (FY22) and +20% (FY20), evidencing very limited pricing power and high operating leverage that cuts both ways
Single product family dependency -- BLIS K12/M18 (and derivatives) are effectively the entire commercial base; no meaningfully diversified pipeline of new strains generating revenue today
Small absolute scale limits R&D, marketing and regulatory investment relative to global probiotics ingredient suppliers

Nano-cap illiquidity: ~1.28bn shares at a low absolute share price (~1.6-1.8 cents) means the NZ$0.001 minimum tick size is a material proportion (roughly 6-8%) of the share price itself, materially raising effective trading costs and price granularity/noise
No dividend paid; company retains all earnings under a full-reinvestment strategy, so there is no income return to offset equity risk

growth_drivers: Expanded Probi AB agreement (Oct 2025) adds pet nutrition as a new licensed category across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets -- a genuinely new addressable market riding on Probi's existing commercial infrastructure

Offline professional health channel expansion by BLIS's Chinese private-label partner -- private label revenue grew 67% in FY26 to $1.3m as the partner invests in health-professional education and offline distribution, a structurally different (and potentially more durable) China growth path than the declining CBEC/daigou channel

China regulatory pathway progressing to examination stage for BLIS K12/M18, with a pivotal clinical trial begun in 2H26 (due to complete 1H27) -- if successful, opens a large, currently under-monetised consumer market on a compliant footing rather than via grey-market resellers
New Zealand wholesale/pharmacy and dental SKU ranging showing strong repeat-purchase economics and continued shelf-space wins
Two new patents granted in FY26 (antiviral applications, prebiotic-sugar combination formulations) opening new product development avenues in immunity and broader health categories beyond oral care
FDA 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS) update for BLIS K12 (May 2026) supports continued/expanded US market access
B Corp certification process underway, which management frames as supporting brand differentiation and stakeholder trust, though this is a soft rather than financial driver

business.description: The three largest customers generated ~54% of FY26 revenue ($7.99m of $14.67m). Probi AB -- simultaneously BLIS's largest licensed distribution partner, a 12.99% shareholder, and board-represented via CEO Anita Johansen -- alone contributed $2.34m of related-party revenue in FY26. Loss, renegotiation, or a change in strategy at any of these counterparties (particularly Probi, which has been steadily converting from ingredient purchaser to royalty payer as it internalises manufacturing) would be highly damaging and BLIS has limited practical ability to negotiate at arm's length given the governance overlap.

Commercial success rests almost entirely on the BLIS K12/M18 strain family; there is no meaningfully monetised pipeline of alternative strains today. A new competing strain, a safety/efficacy controversy, or a shift in consumer/scientific preference away from oral-cavity probiotics would remove the company's entire commercial basis.

EBITDA margin has ranged from -24% (FY22) to +20% (FY20) over FY19-26 and was only 6% in FY26 (8% underlying, ex the $0.9m one-off cost). FY22-23 were loss-making at the EBITDA and NPAT level despite growing revenue in some of those years, showing the cost base does not flex down as readily as revenue can fall -- high operating leverage that has historically worked against shareholders as often as for them.

Reliance on one New Zealand-based fermentation supplier caused a disclosed $0.9m one-off cost increase in FY26 that materially depressed reported EBITDA; technology transfer to an offshore back-up supplier is underway but not complete.

business.risk: IP protection is a mix of patents, trademarks and trade secrets, not a single strong barrier
business.description: The FY26 resolution of the Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan dispute (ending in joint patent ownership rather than BLIS's sole ownership) illustrates that BLIS's patent estate is contestable and does not guarantee exclusivity; competitors and even historical customers can develop or acquire rights to adjacent IP.

financial.risk: Negative FY26 operating cash flow despite positive NPAT
financial.description: Cash generated from operations was $(0.6)m in FY26 versus NPAT of $0.7m, driven by an $862k inventory build (raw materials nearly tripled as BLIS pre-purchased stock around the disclosed supply-chain cost increase) and a $984k increase in trade receivables. Cash and short-term deposits fell from $9.7m to $8.5m over the year. While this appears to be a working-capital timing issue rather than a structural cash burn, the FY26 cash-conversion ratio of -64% (versus +178% in FY25) underlines how volatile and unpredictable cash generation is at this scale, and the trend statement shows negative operating cash flow in three of the last eight years (FY19, FY22, FY26).

At a share price around NZ$0.016-0.018 with 1.279 billion shares on issue (market cap roughly NZ$20-23m), the standard NZX $0.001 minimum price increment represents 5-6% of the share price -- a structurally large bid-ask spread/step that materially widens effective trading costs, discourages institutional participation, and can produce outsized percentage price swings on thin volume.

financial.risk: No dividend and reliance on continued capital discipline
financial.description: Full-reinvestment policy means shareholders rely entirely on capital appreciation; with $8.5m cash and short-term deposits and no debt the balance sheet is solid, but there is no income cushion and the $4.3m unrecognised deferred tax asset (from $14.5m of gross tax losses) will only be realised if the company sustains profitability.

regulatory.description: BLIS's China regulatory pathway for K12/M18 remains mid-process (progressed to 'examination stage' in FY26, with a pivotal clinical trial begun in 2H26 and due to complete 1H27); approval timing and outcome are not guaranteed, and the interim reliance on cross-border e-commerce/daigou channels is itself being deliberately wound back (CBEC revenue nearly halved from $0.6m to $0.3m in FY26), creating a gap between the old China model and the new compliant one.

Amazon US revenue grew despite 'the increased tariff' per the FY26 Chair/CEO letter, and management stated minimal economic loss to date from Middle East conflict-related uncertainty, but ongoing US tariff policy is an explicit, acknowledged cost pressure on BLIS's direct-to-consumer US business.

regulatory.risk: Health/nutraceutical product liability and regulatory approval risk generally
regulatory.description: As a seller of health supplements and conductor of clinical trials, BLIS is exposed to product liability claims and the risk of losing regulatory approval to market/sell in specific countries, both explicitly identified as principal risks in the FY26 governance disclosures.

macro.description: Revenue is predominantly export-derived (85% of FY26 revenue from outside New Zealand) and denominated in USD, EUR and other currencies against an NZD cost base and functional currency; a 10% adverse FX move was modelled to reduce FY26 pre-tax surplus by $29k (disclosed sensitivity), and BLIS uses limited forward FX cover without formal hedge accounting.

B2C revenue (~32% of total) is exposed to discretionary consumer spending on wellness/health supplements, which can soften in a weaker macro/consumer environment, particularly in the price-sensitive Amazon/US direct channel.

Manufacturing, R&D and corporate costs are NZD-denominated in a small domestic economy with a thin specialist labour pool (fermentation science, regulatory affairs) that could face wage inflation pressure disproportionate to global peers with larger operations.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global probiotics/nutraceutical demand continues to grow structurally on consumer interest in gut, oral and immune health, but the industry is increasingly commoditised at the ingredient level with well-funded global players (Novonesis/Chr. Hansen, IFF/Danisco, Lallemand) competing on scale, cost and breadth of strain portfolios. BLIS's oral-cavity probiotic niche remains differentiated by its clinical evidence base but is small relative to the broader probiotics category.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate. B2C wellness/supplement spending has some discretionary sensitivity to consumer confidence; B2B ingredient revenue depends on customers' own order cycles and can be lumpy quarter to quarter (e.g. FY26 EMEA growth was partly attributed to order timing/shorter reorder cycles from one major customer), adding volatility beyond pure end-market demand cycles.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low direct sensitivity given no debt, but BLIS earns meaningful interest income on its ~$8.5m cash/short-term deposit balance ($263k in FY26, down from $428k in FY25 as NZ rates eased and cash was drawn down) -- a modest earnings tailwind/headwind depending on the rate cycle.
key_input_costs: Fermentation/manufacturing (raw materials and consumables rose to $4.13m in FY26 from $2.56m, the single largest driver of margin compression, including the disclosed $0.9m one-off cost increase)
Marketing/advertising spend to support B2C brand awareness and Amazon advertising efficiency
Clinical trial and regulatory costs (China pathway, new product development)
Skilled scientific/regulatory affairs staff in a thin NZ labour market

recent_developments.event: BLIS celebrated its 25th anniversary; shareholders approved constitutional amendments at the Annual Shareholders' Meeting to support the company's B Corp certification pathway

Patent dispute with Bluestone Pharma GmbH (BSP) and Lactosan GmbH & Co. KG resolved: relevant patent applications became jointly owned by BLIS and BSP, all claims between the parties released, and a five-year extension to the existing European supply agreement was renegotiated, providing commercial continuity for the European ingredient relationship
Dame Alison Stewart assumed the role of Chair (following Geoff Plunket's retirement as Chair, and later as a director in March 2026)

Revised Technology Licence and Distribution Agreement with Probi AB announced: extends Probi's exclusive rights to BLIS K12 and BLIS M18 across the USA, Canada and certain EMEA markets, and for the first time adds pet nutrition to Probi's licensed territories

H1 FY26 (six months to 30 September 2025) results released: revenue $7.7m (+28% YoY), EBITDA $0.5m ($1.3m underlying, ex a disclosed $0.8m one-off supply chain cost increase), B2B revenue $5.3m (+39%), B2C revenue $2.4m (+10%); management guided full-year FY26 revenue growth of 10-15% on FY25 (actual FY26 growth came in at 16%, above the top of this range)
Paul Munro (former CEO of Christchurch City Holdings Limited, ex-Deloitte Corporate Finance Partner) appointed as an Independent Non-Executive Director
BLIS K12 received a 'Letter of No Objection' (GRAS self-affirmation confirmation) from the US FDA, reinforcing US market access for the ingredient

FY26 audited annual results released: revenue $14.668m (+16% YoY), reported EBITDA $0.9m (6% margin), underlying EBITDA $1.8m (+83% YoY, ex the $0.9m one-off supply chain cost), NPAT $0.7m (underlying NPAT $1.6m, +90% YoY), cash and short-term deposits $8.5m (down from $9.7m), cash generated from operations NEGATIVE $(0.6)m (driven by inventory build and receivables growth)

BLIS set its 2026 AGM for 27 August 2026 (Dunedin Public Art Gallery, with virtual option), with resolutions including the election of Paul Munro and a proposed increase in the aggregate director remuneration pool from $309,000 to $340,000 per annum following external benchmarking

guidance.as_of: FY26 Annual Report (20 May 2026) and H1 FY26 half-year report (26 November 2025)

items.metric: Revenue growth (FY26, historical guidance already resolved)
items.vs_prior: achieved -- actual FY26 growth of 16% came in above the top end of the previously guided 10-15% range
items.notes: Guidance given at H1 FY26 (November 2025); FY26 actual revenue of $14.668m was +16.0% on FY25's $12.644m

items.metric: FY27 outlook (qualitative, no specific numeric target disclosed)
items.target: Continued growth via key market focus, joint business plans with Probi, and profitable/disciplined growth
items.vs_prior: no specific new numeric guidance issued as of the FY26 annual report
items.notes: Management's FY26 outlook statement said BLIS 'enters FY27 with confidence,' citing strengthened partnerships and growing B2B momentum, but stopped short of a specific revenue, EBITDA or margin target for FY27. Priorities cited: accelerating growth in key markets/joint business plans, supporting China regulatory and clinical milestones, advancing R&D/IP protection, and using the BLIS brand refresh to build consumer awareness, while maintaining financial discipline

items.target: Approximately $0.1m of further one-off costs expected to be released
items.notes: Disclosed at H1 FY26 alongside the $0.8-0.9m one-off cost recognised; implies a small further drag before the cost issue is fully resolved

guidance.management_commentary: Chair Dame Alison Stewart and CEO Scott Johnson: 'We enter FY27 with confidence. The combination of strengthened partnerships with our key business partners and growing B2B momentum provides a solid commercial foundation... We will maintain financial discipline and focus on delivering sustainable, profitable growth.' Management explicitly flagged minimal economic impact to date from Middle East conflict-related macro uncertainty and does not currently foresee material change. No formal FY27 revenue, margin or EBITDA guidance range has been issued as of the FY26 annual report or the most recent NZX announcements found.

bull_case: Genuine, differentiated scientific/IP base (20 publications relating to BLIS strains in FY26 alone, two new patents granted, 25-year clinical track record) that a purely commodity ingredient supplier would lack, supporting premium positioning in oral-health probiotics

Debt-free balance sheet with $8.5m cash and short-term deposits against a market cap of roughly NZ$20-23m -- cash covers over a third of the market capitalisation, and a $4.3m unrecognised tax-loss asset provides a multi-year tax shield if sustained profitability is achieved

The Probi AB relationship, despite its concentration risk, gives BLIS access to a much larger partner's commercial infrastructure across the USA, Canada and EMEA, now extended into a new pet-nutrition adjacency, plus alignment of interests given Probi's 13% shareholding and board seat

FY26 revenue growth of 16% beat the top end of management's own 10-15% guidance range, and underlying EBITDA nearly doubled (+83%) once the one-off supply chain cost is excluded, suggesting real operating leverage exists once cost pressures normalise

Multiple option-value catalysts in progress -- China regulatory/clinical approval (trial due to complete 1H27), pet nutrition category expansion, and continued patent grants -- any one of which could be a step-change in addressable market if successful
bear_case: Eight years of revenue growth from $8.2m to $14.7m (roughly 9% CAGR) has not translated into consistent profitability: EBITDA margin was negative in FY22-23 and only 6% in FY26, and reported NPAT of $0.4-1.6m across FY19-26 has never demonstrated a durable, scalable earnings trajectory -- this reads as a chronically sub-scale business, not an emerging growth story

Extreme customer/related-party concentration: the top three customers are ~54% of revenue, and the single largest commercial partner (Probi AB) is simultaneously a ~13% shareholder with a board seat, creating both a governance conflict-of-interest and a structural risk that BLIS's best territories (North America, key EMEA markets) are being progressively ceded to a partner who is also internalising manufacturing away from BLIS

FY26 cash generated from operations was NEGATIVE $(0.6)m despite positive NPAT, driven by inventory build and receivables growth -- a reminder that reported profit at this scale can diverge sharply from actual cash generation, and cash/short-term deposits fell $1.2m over the year

Nano-cap illiquidity (market cap ~NZ$20-23m, share price ~1.6-1.8 cents against 1.28bn shares) with a $0.001 minimum tick representing 5-6% of the share price itself, materially widening effective trading costs and discouraging institutional ownership

Single product-family dependency on BLIS K12/M18 with no meaningfully monetised alternative-strain pipeline, combined with a track record of patent/IP disputes (the FY26 Bluestone Pharma/Lactosan resolution ended in shared rather than exclusive ownership) that shows the IP moat is contestable rather than absolute

No dividend, thin trading liquidity, and management's own FY27 outlook offers no specific numeric guidance -- investors are asked to underwrite continued execution on qualitative promises (China approval, Probi joint business plans, brand refresh) rather than a committed financial target
